newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand launches tapioca price support scheme.
newsitem.headline: Thailand launches tapioca price support scheme.

text.p: The Thai government on Thursday started a 2.98 billion baht ($114 million) tapioca price support scheme in response to a recent protest by cassava planters, a Commerce Ministry official said.
The scheme, being implemented until April 30, calls for the government to pay compensation to tapioca producers who buy cassava roots from planters at guaranteed prices.
The govenment required producers participating in the programme to buy cassava roots at one baht/kg, regardless of starch content, and chips at 2.46 baht/kg.
The programme was opposed by some tapioca producers and exporters as impractical.
"Although we are compensated for buying at guaranteed prices, I still think this is not a practical measure," said a source at the Thai Tapioca Trade Association.

"The government should encourage farmers to produce better quality roots, which will cut production costs and fetch more money, instead of using price intervention, which distorts the real cost," he said.
They said cassava roots fetching one baht/kg should carry at least 25 percent starch content.
But the Commerce Ministry official defended the plan, saying it was a short-term measure while the govenment works on new high yield strains to help boost output.
